pr.title: Build and find stacks with gh stack, and fall back to base branches without it
pr.head: 2bb868241e49d7c3501582a477fc32c58b4c22e9

summary: Projector's skills tell an agent how to build a change (implement), how to answer review findings on it (fix-pr), and how to keep doing that across many pull requests (start-fix-loop). When a change is too big for one review, the agent splits it into a stack: a chain of pull requests, each based on the branch of the one below it, that GitHub records as one stack. GitHub only records the chain when it is made with gh stack, a GitHub CLI extension that Projector documents in its vendored skills/gh-stack/SKILL.md.

Before this change, only implement pointed at that extension. fix-pr said to use "the installed stack workflow" without naming it, start-fix-loop grouped a stack's pull requests without saying how to find them, and no skill said what to do when the extension is missing. In practice, agents chained pull requests with gh pr create --base, which GitHub does not record as a stack.

This change gives implement one section, "Stack dependent work", that names the gh stack commands for each task and one fallback for when gh stack cannot help. Inside a stack that gh stack works on, a layer takes in its base only by rebasing, because gh stack has no option to merge. A chain without gh stack is updated by merging, so it needs no force-push. The other skills point at that section. The rule also goes into the section that project init writes into every adopting repository's AGENTS.md, whose template moves to version 2.

cards.title: When a skill falls back to base branches
cards.html:
• gh extension list shows no github/gh-stack.
  • A gh stack command exits 9, which means the repository does not have stacks enabled.
  • The stacks API, repos/<owner>/<repo>/stacks?pull_request=<n>, returns an error or [].

The fallback reads the chain from each pull request's base branch, opens layers with gh pr create --draft --base, and updates layers by merging each into the one above it. The agent tells the user at most once, and never installs the extension.

cards.title: What the review found
cards.html:
• Four heads reviewed, and a re-review of this head after the author rewrote the description. All three findings are fixed: a rebased stack layer is gated before it is pushed, AGENTS.md no longer says to rebase where the skills merge, and the description now matches this head. The last review is clean.
  • The command names, flags, exit code 9, and cited section names match skills/gh-stack/SKILL.md and gh stack v0.1.0's --help.
  • 531 tests, project check, and both claude plugin validate runs pass at this head.

groups.title: One place that says how to stack
groups.kicker: The new "Stack dependent work" section in implement, which every other skill now cites
intro: implement is the skill an agent follows to build a change and open its pull request. Its new "Stack dependent work" section is the reference the rest of this pull request points at. It covers four tasks, each first with gh stack and then without it.

TaskWith gh stackWithout it
Create a stackinit, add, then submit --auto, which opens draftsgit push -u, then gh pr create --draft --base per layer
Adopt an existing chaingh stack link with the pull request numbers, bottom firstNot needed
Update the layers: carry a fix up, take in the default branch, or catch up after a layer mergesgh stack rebase (--upstack from a fixed layer), run the gate on each rewritten layer, then gh stack push; never a mergeMerge each layer into the one above it, from the bottom up, running the gate before each push
Find the layersThe stacks API, or gh stack view --json in a checkout that tracks the stackFollow base branches with gh pr list --head and --base
The section keeps the mechanics of each command in skills/gh-stack/SKILL.md, which this pull request does not change.

files.note: Adds the "Stack dependent work" section, links to it from the sizing rule, and says to replace the body gh stack submit writes.

checks.text: The stacks API behaves as described. stacks?pull_request=196 returned stack 199 with pull requests 196 and 197 from the bottom up, including merged ones. stacks?pull_request=215 returned [], and so did the same query against cli/cli, a repository without stacks, rather than an error.

The gate now runs before the push. The bullet rebases, runs the full gate on every layer the rebase rewrote, and only then runs gh stack push. It uses gh stack rebase rather than gh stack sync after a layer merges, because sync pushes as part of the same command. skills/gh-stack/SKILL.md confirms that rebase detects a merged pull request and replays the layers above it with --onto.
The layers above a pull request come one level at a time: gh pr list --base <headRefName> finds the direct child, and the agent repeats the lookup from that child's head branch to reach the top.

Without gh stack, a chain is updated by merging rather than rebasing, the same way fix-pr updates any branch. A merge needs no force-push, so review threads stay anchored, and fix-pr's force-push rule now allows a force-push only through gh stack or where the repository's instructions call for a rebase.

files.note: Checks that the template, fix-pr, and start-fix-loop each cite "Stack dependent work", and that implement has that heading.

groups.title: Fixing and grouping stacked pull requests
groups.kicker: fix-pr and start-fix-loop now name gh stack and cite the implement section
intro: fix-pr answers review findings and resolves merge conflicts on one pull request. start-fix-loop watches many pull requests and gives each one, or each stack, a subagent that runs fix-pr. Both used to describe stacks vaguely. Now both cite the "Stack dependent work" section for how to find a stack's layers and how to carry a fix up through them.

The main behavior change is in fix-pr's conflict handling. For an ordinary pull request, or a chain without gh stack, it still merges the base, because a merge needs no force-push. For a layer of a stack that gh stack works on, step 1 runs gh stack rebase and pushes nothing, step 3 runs the gate on every layer the rebase rewrote, and step 4 pushes them with gh stack push. Its force-push rule now allows a force-push only through gh stack, or to resolve a conflict where the repository's instructions call for a rebase.

files.note: Updates a conflicted stack layer by gh stack's rebase and pushes it after the gate, carries fixes up through the implement section, and narrows the force-push rule.

checks.text: The finding from the first head is fixed. Step 1 runs only gh stack rebase and pushes nothing (line 105), step 3 runs the gate on every rewritten layer, and this step pushes with gh stack push once the gate passes.

After a parent merges, the layers above are updated by the same rebase, not by gh stack sync, so the gate still runs before anything is pushed. Without gh stack, a squash-merged parent's new base is merged into the child.

files.note: Finds a stack's layers, and groups pull requests into one subagent per stack, with the implement section's lookup.

groups.title: The generated Projector section
groups.kicker: The stack rule moves into the AGENTS.md section that project init writes, as template version 2
intro: Every repository that adopts Projector has a section in its AGENTS.md, between projector:begin and projector:end markers, that project init writes from src/projector/templates/agents-block.md. The number in the begin marker is the template version. project check warns when a repository's section is older than the template the CLI ships, and project init refreshes it without touching anything outside the markers.

This head adds one paragraph to that template: open dependent work as a stack with gh stack, let gh stack carry a fix up by rebasing, and chain by base branch and merge only where gh stack is unavailable. The version moves from 1 to 2, and tests/test_instructions.py pins the new text's hash. This repository's own AGENTS.md drops its two hand-written stack sentences and carries the refreshed section. docs/cli.md lists the new topic, and docs/plugins.md tells a plugin user that the extension is optional.

checks.text: project check at this head prints no warning about the Projector section, so this repository's AGENTS.md block matches the version 2 template. A repository still on version 1 gets an instructions-outdated warning, not an error.

files.note: Adds the stack paragraph and bumps the template to version 2.
